newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-MPs agree to benefits for jobseekers abroad.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs agree to benefits for jobseekers abroad.

text.p: Plans to allow the unemployed to seek work in other European Union countries without losing their social security benefits won the support of the European Parliament on Tuesday.
The European Commission is proposing to modify a 1971 regulation which allows the jobless to seek work abroad for up to three months.
Under the proposal -- COM(95)734 -- jobseekers will be able to remain abroad longer, with the host country taking over responsibility for paying their benefits after three months.
To benefit from the new rules, jobhunters will have to sign on within seven days of arriving in the member state concerned.

In a move to prevent so-called benefit tourism, the Commission recommends that if people move to a member state which offers higher or more long-term benefits, they should only receive the level of benefits applying in their home country.
